races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Basilano
runners_data.note: Exposed form (0-8-8) at a higher level over six and eight furlongs is a concern; a natural closer by preference but, with the rear already crowded, will likely end up in midfield rather than getting a clear back-straight position — style fit is materially compromised.|

runners_data.name: In The Gloaming
runners_data.note: Has gone 5-6 twice on Good going, which is at least evidence of some aptitude for conditions, but a hold-up runner by nature who will struggle to find a clear passage late in a 14-runner field where genuine closers are already displaced.|

runners_data.name: Banish Misfortune
runners_data.note: Older at four and consistently finishing well down the field (best recent finish 8th); true hold-up style sits awkwardly in this race shape, and the fade flag here is a significant concern over a flat five furlongs at the sharp end of the contest.|

runners_data.name: Forza Magico
runners_data.note: Two starts both on Good ground over six furlongs, finishing 2nd and 5th — drop to five is the unknown, but natural prominent style is ideally suited to this pace scenario and trainer Feane runs a second horse here (Tudor Flame), suggesting stable confidence.|

runners_data.name: Gaineamh Min
runners_data.note: Single run, 12th of 14 over six furlongs on Good, and carries the fade flag — very little to recommend positionally or on form, and the step up to a bigger field on the sharp five makes improvement hard to project.|

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Best form a second place at the Curragh on Soft/Standard over five furlongs; the fade flag is a mild concern but prominent style and jockey Ben Coen give her tactical options, and Good ground at Down Royal suits.|

runners_data.name: Orellana
runners_data.note: Debut run was 10th over eight furlongs on Good — unknown style, lightly raced flag, drop in trip significant; Siobhan Rutledge is a capable apprentice but there is too little evidence to assess whether five furlongs on turf suits.|

runners_data.name: Osterode
runners_data.note: Wearing a visor, trained by the in-form McCreery yard (7 winners from 22 in 14 days), and shaped respectably with a 4th and 5th over five furlongs — hold-up style is moderate but the headgear change and trainer form are genuine positives.|

runners_data.name: Otsana
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; single run was a fifth over seven furlongs on Good, suggesting she has the cruising speed to lead over five — W.J. Lee takes the ride and Twomey has shown faith with this filly.|

runners_data.name: Sarfarcat
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the lower half of the field over seven and eight furlongs, with one 6th as best effort; hold-up style and a fade flag make her chances remote in a race that rewards prominent racers.|

runners_data.name: Sassy Boom
runners_data.note: 182 days off the track, has a tongue-tie, and her best form has been 8th, 10th, 10th and 12th on varying going — combination of layoff, headgear and poor recent form makes her very difficult to support.|

runners_data.name: Tudor Flame
runners_data.note: Debutant with no recorded history and unknown going preference — trained by the same Feane yard as Forza Magico; only the paddock and early market moves will reveal anything meaningful here.|

runners_data.name: Famed Again
runners_data.note: Best piece of form is a 5th over seven furlongs on Good; natural hold-up runner shifted to midfield by the field's composition, and the seven-to-eight furlong trip profile suggests five furlongs may be too sharp regardless of position.|

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at five furlongs (4th on Standard, 4th on Good) so the trip and going are not a concern — but a natural closer mapped forward in a field with limited hold-up room, and the style_fit discount must temper any enthusiasm.|

races.paceDynamic: Otsana is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner maiden and, with no horse capable of seriously pressuring her for the lead, she should dictate a controlled, even gallop from the outset on Good turf at Down Royal. With Forza Magico and Kiss Don't Tell likely to track from prominent positions, the pace will be genuine but not scorching — a sustainable rhythm that keeps the race compressed until the final furlong. The redistribution note is important here: Basilano, Banish Misfortune, In The Gloaming, Famed Again and White Smoke are all natural hold-up horses that cannot all sit where they want in a 14-runner field, meaning the race will be more congested in midfield than the pace map suggests and genuine late closers will face a traffic puzzle. This race shape — an uncontested leader setting a moderate-to-fair pace on fast ground over five furlongs — strongly favours horses able to travel prominently and quicken in the straight, with the lead or close-up positions giving a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Otsana Leads Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Otsana bowls along comfortably in front and the pace remains controlled throughout the five furlongs.
scenarios.body: Otsana sets a sustainable gallop with no serious challenger for the lead, meaning horses that travel close to the pace have the clearest run and first run on the field; the final furlong becomes a test of finishing quality from the front two or three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves just fast enough to string the field out and a prominent racer produces a decisive move entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Horses like Forza Magico and Kiss Don't Tell, sitting a length or two off the leader with clear daylight, benefit most when the tempo stretches the hold-up horses out of contention; the winner comes from the top four or five early positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and congestion allows a horse mapped centrally to thread through late.
scenarios.body: Osterode, wearing a visor and trained by the in-form McCreery yard, is best placed of those in midfield to benefit from a sudden opening, while In The Gloaming could also get a late run if traffic clears; this scenario depends on the front runners weakening sharply, which is not the typical shape here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is surprisingly strong and the front runners tie up in the closing stages, allowing genuine hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the true hold-up horses — Basilano, Banish Misfortune, Famed Again and White Smoke — are all redistributed and unlikely to sit where they need to in order to finish with full effect; their style_fit discounts are significant and the short five-furlong trip over good ground rarely suits waiting tactics.

watchPoints.text: Osterode — McCreery yard in blistering form (7/22 in 14 days), visor applied for the first time, and two solid efforts over five furlongs; if she travels smoothly in midfield she is the most dangerous horse outside the front group.
Tudor Flame — debutant from the Feane yard, which also runs the prominent Forza Magico; watch early market activity and paddock behaviour to gauge how seriously the stable is running this horse.

Otsana's early fractions — if W.J. Lee is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged, the winning distance could be significant; watch whether Kiss Don't Tell or Forza Magico attempt to close up early and apply any pressure to the pace.

Redistribution effect — with Basilano, Banish Misfortune, Famed Again, White Smoke and In The Gloaming all crowding towards midfield rather than settling at the rear, expect significant bunching on the back straight and potential interference entering the final furlong.

Sassy Boom — 182 days absent, tongue-tie applied; monitor in the ring for signs of freshness or if the market firms unexpectedly, as an O'Connell-trained runner can occasionally spring a surprise fresh.

races.name: Grant Thornton Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Someday Somewhere
runners_data.note: Unbeaten style of hold-up form but has shown the ability to race prominently when required; placed on all four good-ground starts (sim-going 4/4) and the step back to 7f from 8f should suit, making this one of the more reliable profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Romance
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with headgear noted; goes well on good ground (2/3 sim-going) but her sole soft-ground run saw her finish tenth — conditions today are fine; Andrew Slattery takes the ride and she's entitled to improve third time out over 7f.

runners_data.name: Arizonaneargalway
runners_data.note: A consistent back-marker who has returned figures of 10, 8, 8, 13 on good ground across her four starts — the fade warning is backed by every run in her form; Mel Sheridan claims 7lb but the raw form suggests a horse struggling to raise her game.

runners_data.name: Summer Sent You
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose last three runs on good ground all ended in fades — the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the overcrowded rear of this field, and racing slightly closer than preferred may not resolve her finishing-kick limitations; treat the STYLE_FIT discount as meaningful here.

runners_data.name: Thelymitra
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien runner returning after 38 days off with blinkers applied on this occasion; all three career starts have come on good ground over 7f-8f and she has posted respectable sixth, eighth and eleventh placings without threatening — the freshness angle is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Fine Line
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan-trained hold-up type whose best effort (4th) came over 8f on good ground; redistributed into a midfield slot because true rear-of-field positions are oversubscribed, and Reese Holohan's 7lb claim helps, but the form profile (0-0-0-7-4) shows progress is slow.

runners_data.name: Elyatta
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this Noel Meade two-year-old who ran just six days ago — the quick turnaround warrants monitoring; blinkers applied, and the 4th on good ground over 7f last time is the standout run; a natural closer who is mapped to midfield because the hold-up spots are saturated in this field.

runners_data.name: Dear Theodosia
runners_data.note: The only horse performing a confirmed pace-setting role in this race, but that role is manufactured — she is a natural hold-up or prominent type pushed to the front because no true front-runner entered; Ben Coen is an elite booking and may help mask the style mismatch, but the STYLE_FIT reduction of 0.80 is a legitimate concern over the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Ballymackney
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes rides this Noel Meade inmate who hasn't raced for 43 days; her best turf form came over 5f-8f on good ground but the nursery mark of 54 and persistent fade pattern across three career starts leave little to work with, even accounting for a fresh return.

runners_data.name: Rathbran Lady
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's yard is in decent 14-day form (2/13); this filly steps up to 7f from 6f and her form figures of 7, 10, 12 across three runs include only two on good ground — Wesley Joyce claims 3lb and she's lightly weighted at OR 52, but the raw form offers limited encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Dear Theodosia is the one confirmed pace-setter in this 10-runner 7f nursery handicap at Down Royal, redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up style — she will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop on good ground with no genuine rival prepared to push her hard from the outset. The absence of a true front-runner means the pace is likely to be moderate and controlled, creating a race that develops into a prolonged stamina test in the final two furlongs rather than a sprint finish off a strong tempo. Summer Sent You, Fine Line, Elyatta, Ballymackney and Rathbran Lady are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield positions because there are simply too many hold-up horses in this field to accommodate their natural late-running roles. This race shape, with an uncontested moderate lead and a cluster of horses that prefer to come from behind all fighting for the same ground, strongly favours the few runners who can sit close to the pace without being asked to lead — Someday Somewhere and Romance are the profiles best equipped to exploit a steady tempo and hit the front at the right moment.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Closers Denied
scenarios.trigger: If Dear Theodosia controls a moderate pace and the midfield hold-up pack find traffic or lack a meaningful late surge.
scenarios.body: Dear Theodosia's uncontested lead on good ground sets a rhythm that suits horses racing prominently, and those sitting a length or two off the pace in the first half of the field can pounce without needing a strong gallop to close the gap; the hold-up brigade, though numerous, are largely redistributed and likely to find each other in the way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the final three furlongs to string the field out and open clear daylight for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A sharper mid-race tempo would create the gaps the genuine hold-up types need, and one of the better-rated closers finding a run on the outside could arrive with a sustained late challenge; with several horses competing for the same late-running position, however, this requires near-perfect execution and a clear passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Injected, Front Falls Away
scenarios.trigger: If Dear Theodosia's manufactured lead collapses in the final furlong as her out-of-role front-running exacts a stamina toll.
scenarios.body: A horse who has been dictating against her natural instincts is vulnerable to tying up late, and a prominent racer able to maintain momentum through the final two furlongs could sweep past a faltering leader; this is a genuine risk given Dear Theodosia's STYLE_FIT penalty and her limited experience of making the running.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace bunches the field into a tight group at the two-furlong pole and the race degenerates into a sprint finish with multiple challengers hitting the line together.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo can paradoxically produce a messy, compressed finish where positional advantage and draw matter as much as ability; in a race this loaded with hold-up types forced out of role, the chaotic shape could see a lightly-weighted, fresh horse emerge from the scrum.

watchPoints.text: Dear Theodosia is racing out of her natural style on the lead — watch whether Ben Coen can sustain the gallop after the 2f pole or if she visibly ties up and surrenders a front she was never meant to hold.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Summer Sent You, Fine Line, Elyatta, Ballymackney, Rathbran Lady) will all be hunting the same late ground — watch for a traffic-jam scenario down the outside in the final quarter mile that prevents any one closer from landing a clean blow.

Someday Somewhere's consistent placed form on good ground at this trip makes her the standout positional fit for the expected moderate pace — watch whether Jack Kearney (3) gets her to travel close enough to the leader to pounce early in the straight.

Elyatta ran just six days ago — watch for any signs of residual fatigue in the early exchanges, as a horse carrying that quick turnaround and asked to race out of her natural rear position may not fire as fully as her last-run form implies.

Thelymitra returns after 38 days with blinkers fitted for the first time — watch how she jumps and settles, as the headgear change and layoff combined could produce either a bold forward move or an unsettled early performance that kills her chance before the race develops.

races.name: Grant Thornton Ulster Cesarewitch Handicap

runners_data.name: Ragmans Corner
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good and placed over 16f on Heavy recently — proven stamina and course-trip form; hold-up style but with a big-field win on the board suggests he knows how to find his way through traffic.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Won last time over 16f on Soft and has course-winning form; hold-up type who may get further back than ideal in this big field, headgear tongue-tie worn, Adam Caffrey takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Happy Jacky
runners_data.note: Prominent style is an asset in a race dominated by hold-up horses; 12-year-old veteran with strong place record over staying trips on Good ground, though 56 days off is worth noting for a horse whose trainer has had a quiet 14-day spell.

runners_data.name: Trubshaw
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner; won over 14f on Good last time for De Bromhead's hot yard (T14: 6/29), wears blinkers, and with no pace rival will control the tempo — the key horse in the shape of this race.

runners_data.name: Zoffman
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader in the finish — hold-up style who carries the warning label that he often does not see out his races; 4 days since last run (very quick turnaround) and recent form figures of 68030 do not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Feud
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with an inconsistent form string over staying trips; best placed on Good ground over marathon distances but recent figures (30/40-) suggest he needs things to fall right and is unreliable.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up racer by nature, though positioned in midfield on the map because this field is stacked with closers; has course and distance form (won 20f, placed 22f on Good), wears tongue-tie and blinkers — jockey Gary Carroll may push for a more prominent early position than the horse typically finds.

runners_data.name: Sign From Above
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural position is near the rear, but with Ben Coen aboard he has the jockey quality to negotiate a clear run from midfield; no wins from 12 tries on Good ground is the concerning stat (0W1P), wears blinkers.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: True hold-up type by record but finds himself mapped further forward than he would naturally go; W J Lee rides, and recent form (95765) over a variety of trips on Good suggests he is consistent without threatening to win.

runners_data.name: Banana Three
runners_data.note: Placed four times over staying distances on Good ground without winning; natural rear-of-field runner shifted to midfield on the map — headgear (p) worn, trainer had one winner from 21 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Cozone
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with an excellent record of winning over staying trips including a course win over 18f; hold-up style by nature but has the class to slot in midfield — note the very quick turnaround (4 days since last run) and the tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Alba Chiara
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old stepping well up in trip and weight class; form figures of 2-0004 suggest she has been struggling, and her best efforts came over 13f on Good rather than the marathon 2m2½f — distance is a significant query.

runners_data.name: Gangster Granny
runners_data.note: Outstanding course-and-distance record: 4 wins and 5 places over 22f on Good at tracks like this — the most specific form profile in the race for this trip and going; despite being a hold-up type displaced to midfield, Chris Hayes could yet deliver her late if the pace scenario obliges.

runners_data.name: Yogini
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3-year-old trained by O'Brien carrying just 123lbs; only three career runs, all at shorter trips (10-12f), making the jump to 2m2½f a very significant unknown — headgear (tongue-tie and blinkers) worn, 23 days since last run.

runners_data.name: Sanctity Of Space
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) — no jockey declared in the data; form of 424/07 over distances around 14-16f on Good ground, has place form but the style uncertainty and missing jockey information make assessment difficult.

runners_data.name: Deralo Ir
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old whose best efforts came over much shorter trips (10-13f) — the 2m2½f looks like a very significant stamina test based on his history; no trainer jockey listed, form figures of 27-706 are modest.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on Good and placed twice at that trip — shows ability but the step up to 2m2½f is a major stamina leap with no evidence he stays this far; hold-up type whose natural position is further back than the map places him.

races.paceDynamic: Trubshaw is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Gabriella Hill can dictate a controlled, honest gallop over the 2m2½f trip on Good ground at Down Royal. With one horse setting a sustainable tempo unchallenged, the race will be run at a steady-to-moderate clip through the early stages, with the pace likely to increase only from the home turn — a shape that typically rewards those who can track the leader in the first two or three positions and kick off a true gallop. The redistributed hold-up horses — Golden Temple, Sign From Above, Way Down South, Banana Three, Cozone, Alba Chiara, Gangster Granny, Deralo Ir and Cooley's Mist — are genuine late-runners by nature but are mapped to midfield because the field carries far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of these, Golden Temple and Sign From Above are most likely to actually secure prominent ground given their class and jockey quality. The dominant tactical verdict is that prominent racers who can sit just behind Trubshaw and travel through the race will be ideally placed — a slowly-run long-distance handicap on Good ground almost never favours true closers who find themselves mid-to-rear in a compact field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trubshaw Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw sets an uncontested, controlled gallop and the decisive move comes from a horse sitting second or third early.
scenarios.body: Trubshaw bowls along in front, the race stays compressed and the winner comes from the small group tracking the leader into the straight, as the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by a late injection of pace over a trip that rewards those who have been travelling kindly throughout. Horses with the stamina to stay the 2m2½f and the tactical speed to hold a prominent pitch are ideally suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Front Runs Home
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw's gallop is so unchallenged and conservative that no rival can reel her in once she quickens entering the straight.
scenarios.body: With a featherweight tempo through the body of the race, Trubshaw conserves enough energy to simply lengthen and hold on, her 4-year-old freshness on recent winning form proving decisive at this trip on Good ground. Prominent types who track her closely benefit most if Trubshaw does fade, but a wire-to-wire result is entirely plausible under these conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected through the middle stages and the field strings out, giving true hold-up horses room to finish through.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race over 2m2½f on Good ground can stretch the field and allow strong stayers to pick off rivals in the closing stages, though this scenario is tempered because most of the field's hold-up horses are displaced from their natural position and may lack the clear passage they need. Gangster Granny's emphatic course-and-distance winning record and Ragmans Corner's proven stamina make them the most credible beneficiaries even from deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Midfield Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race, the field concertinas and a horse from the central pack produces a winning burst in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start gallop over a long trip often produces a winner from the middle of the field who has avoided trouble and found a clear run late, but this shape is the hardest to engineer in a 17-runner handicap where position is difficult to control. Sign From Above and Boxing Great, both able to travel prominently when the pace is modest, could emerge from the pack if the finish compresses.

watchPoints.text: Trubshaw is unopposed in front and if Gabriella Hill (7lb claim) misjudges the tempo — either going too slow and leaving rivals with no pace to aim at, or injecting a burst too early — it fundamentally alters which profiles can win.

Gangster Granny's four course wins over 22f on Good make her the most form-specific horse in the race for this trip, and if Chris Hayes can extract her from midfield with a clear run she could be the most dangerous late mover.

The very quick turnarounds of Zoffman (4 days) and Cozone (4 days) are notable — horses returning within a week of their last run can be sharper or flatter than normal, and both are worth monitoring in the betting for any market drift.

With nine redistributed hold-up horses all looking for racing room from roughly the same position, traffic and interference entering the straight is a serious risk — back-markers finishing with running left but blocked should be noted for future reference.

Yogini (3yo, O'Brien yard, T14: 2/21) is a jockey-less 3-year-old taking a massive trip rise with no previous evidence of staying 2m2½f — monitor for any significant market move that might suggest connections have found a distance angle not visible in the form.

races.name: Children's Heartbeat Trust Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Solomon Coop
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type returning after 259 days off, with his best form coming over 8-9f on good; the step to 10f-plus and layoff are real concerns, and trainer has no recent winners to give confidence.|

runners_data.name: Areana
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has won twice at 10f on good ground in Ireland and arrives very fresh after 355 days off; though her form is genuinely strong in similar conditions, she is a natural hold-up horse who will be squeezed into midfield in a field with too many closers to find her natural berth, tempering her winning chance.|

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Consistent handicapper in good form (LR 17d, T14 3/17 active trainer) but wears blinkers and is at heart a horse who wants to race from off the pace — in a race where true rear-runners are crowded out, she will need to race closer than ideal to avoid being buried.|

runners_data.name: Doctor Grace
runners_data.note: Has won over 12f on good ground and placed over 10f on the same surface, so the trip and conditions suit; wears a hood and is a hold-up type, but his two recent placings at this distance give him a credible profile even if the race shape is not ideal.|

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: Placed over 11f on good ground last time out just 12 days ago, wears a hood and has legitimate claims at this trip; a genuine hold-up horse who will need to find room in a bunched midfield, but his recent fitness edge over many rivals is a point in his favour.|

runners_data.name: Solomon
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader in finishes, wears a hood-and-tongue-tie combination, and has posted a string of mid-to-rear finishes over 10-12f on soft and standard — good ground on this specific trip has produced his worst efforts and the tendency to fade is a significant negative in a slowly-run race.|

runners_data.name: Berto Ramirez
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a consistent placing profile (four times fourth in recent starts) over 12-17f, mostly on good ground; trainer has no recent winners, and his natural hold-up style places him in exactly the crowded midfield section where clean runs will be hard to find.|

runners_data.name: Daonethatgotaway
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has not scored recently; his last six runs show a single second place, and the hold-up style he favours will see him racing in a cluster of similar horses with no pace to chase — a difficult position to overcome.|

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: The most interesting prominent racer in the race: two wins at 10f on good ground in his last five starts, wears a tongue-strap, trainer active with 1 winner from 28 (T14), and he is one of only two horses genuinely able to race in his natural prominent position close to the pace.|

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: Four-year-old mare with form figures of 7-9-7-5-4 in her last five, all over 10-12f on good-to-soft ground; wears a hood, has not won, and as a hold-up type she will be competing for the same space as a dozen other closers.|

runners_data.name: Lough Leane
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground two runs back, wears a tongue-strap, but has been beaten 15th and 6th since and the layoff is only 32 days; as a rear-runner in a field packed with hold-up types, getting a clear run will be the principal challenge.|

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Wears a visor, with four placings in recent form but no win in six starts; a hold-up racer who has placed at 10-12f on good and standard ground — the visor suggests connections are trying to sharpen a horse who has been consistent without winning.|

runners_data.name: Chosen One
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Donnacha/Aidan O'Brien (T14 2/21), with a second at 10f on good ground on his best day; wears a tongue-strap and has been running in stronger company, which could mean this handicap mark is fair — but the hold-up style puts him in the same traffic problem as most of his rivals.|

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fader at the finish; trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien (T14 13/79, very active); won at 10f on good ground and wears a hood, but the fade flag over this trip is a genuine concern and the congested midfield scenario does not help.|

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field, with two wins and two placings over 10-12f on good ground in her last five starts — she controls this race from flag to finish and the tempo she sets will determine every outcome; trainer has no recent form and the Reserve 1 jockey booking is a slight unknown, but her positional advantage is massive.|

runners_data.name: Good Man Jack
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a string of 7-9-8-9-17 finishes, flagged as a fader, and trainer without recent winners; a hold-up horse who has consistently finished in the rear on good ground and has nothing in his profile to suggest improvement in this larger field.|

runners_data.name: Chestnut Palace
runners_data.note: Trained by Noel Meade (T14 1/28) and wears blinkers; his last five runs all feature placings at 10-12f on good ground and he is one of only two genuine prominent racers who can naturally slot into position behind A Pretty Penny — his consistency without winning is a concern but his race positioning is ideal.|

races.paceDynamic: A Pretty Penny is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 17 and will stride straight to the lead from the gates, setting what figures to be a measured, uncontested pace over 1m2½f on good ground at Down Royal. With no rival willing or able to genuinely challenge for the lead, she is free to dictate her own fractions and will control the tempo from the front, potentially leaving this race run at a steady-to-moderate gallop that flatters those tracking her through the early and middle stages. Hexagonal and Chestnut Palace are the only two genuine prominent types mapped in their natural position, and they will look to settle just behind A Pretty Penny, giving them the best view of proceedings and an ideal jumping-off point in the straight. The field holds a far greater concentration of hold-up horses than can genuinely race from the rear with purpose — Darkdeserthighway, Areana, Solomon, Berto Ramirez, Daonethatgotaway, Enchanted Lady, Lough Leane and others are all natural closers squeezed into a midfield cluster, meaning several will be racing wide or in traffic rather than in their preferred berth, blunting the effectiveness of hold-up tactics. This race shape emphatically favours the prominent-to-front running profile: a steady gallop set by a lone leader benefits those close to the pace rather than deep closers who will struggle to generate the late momentum they need from a congested midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Penny Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If A Pretty Penny controls a steady tempo unchallenged and Hexagonal or Chestnut Palace track close enough to pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: A Pretty Penny sets a comfortable pace that turns this into a tactical affair, meaning the horses closest to her through the race have first run on the field entering the straight; the lack of genuine pace pressure means the lead group do not get strung out, and a prominent racer with enough class can reel her in or kick past in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If A Pretty Penny's fractions are slow enough that she conserves energy throughout and nothing from the chasing pack has sufficient zip to close her down.
scenarios.body: With a solo lead and a steady gallop, A Pretty Penny reaches the straight with a healthy buffer and her good record at this trip on good ground — including two recent wins — means she may simply prove too well positioned to be caught by hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, One Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield cluster produces a clear run for one redistributed hold-up horse who times a late challenge to perfection.
scenarios.body: The compressed nature of the field mid-race means a horse that finds a gap at the right moment — such as Sinbad My Dad or Doctor Grace, who have placed at this sort of distance and trip on similar ground — can thread through and catch the tiring leaders late; however, the redistribution of so many natural closers into the same space makes clean passages the exception rather than the rule.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace set by A Pretty Penny is never fast enough to stretch the field and the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to bridge.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up race in a muddled-pace scenario is the least likely outcome here given the number of redistributed closers who cannot get their natural position and will be racing against their preferred style; horses like Solomon, Good Man Jack and Daonethatgotaway carry explicit fade warnings and the absence of forcing pace means their usual late kicks are severely blunted.

watchPoints.text: A Pretty Penny is the lone front-runner in a field of 17 — watch whether Reserve 1 (unnamed jockey) sets a crawl or a genuine gallop, as the tempo she chooses will entirely determine whether she is caught in the straight or holds on unchallenged.

Hexagonal and Chestnut Palace are the only two genuine prominent types able to race in their natural position; if either is blocked or wide early, the race loses its only credible pressure on the leader from a horse not racing out of role.

At least eight horses flagged as hold-up types are redistributed into midfield — watch for severe traffic and crowding on the turn into the straight, which could cause interference and effectively eliminate several runners from contention regardless of ability.

Sweet Baby Zou and Solomon both carry fade-in-finish flags and are trained by powerful yards (O'Brien / Sweeney); if they appear to travel well into the straight, beware the finishing effort may not materialise as expected.

Areana (355d off) and Solomon Coop (259d off) are very fresh after long absences — watch market moves at the off for either, as supported fitness horses returning from layoffs in Irish handicaps can be especially well-prepared when heavily backed.

races.name: Grant Thornton Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: Won at 14f on good going last time out — best form marker in this field — and Adrian McGuinness's yard has been ticking over; a natural hold-up type who needs the race to be run at a fair clip to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: Plains Indian
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old returning after 445 days off, which is a significant fitness query regardless of ability; hold-up style suits a strong pace that is unlikely to materialise, and the layoff makes him very hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Placed over 18f on good ground in recent form and tongue-tie added; a hold-up runner who needs cover, but the slow likely tempo means he will have to work harder than ideal to land a blow.|

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Dropped out of sprint company to stay-oriented 10f-plus trips, placed twice at 12f on good ground; tongue-tie retained, hold-up style, but the distance step to 1m5f is new territory so stamina must prove out.|

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at distances up to 18f and genuinely a hold-up type by nature, though the map places him in midfield given field composition; at OR 50 the handicapper has him within reach, but the steady pace works against his deeper closing style.|

runners_data.name: Limestone Red
runners_data.note: Form has been at 9f-12f and the jump to 1m5f is a query; a natural rear-of-field runner operating in mid-pack here due to the crowded hold-up brigade — the shorter distance profile is the bigger concern.|

runners_data.name: Quinchy Lady
runners_data.note: Only three career runs, all finishing tailed off at 8f-10f on good ground, fades flag attached; the trip extension to 1m5f represents an unexplored stamina test for a lightly raced three-year-old with no encouraging form to date.|

runners_data.name: Invincible Destiny
runners_data.note: Consistent in the mid-to-low positions on OR 53, but all four recent runs have ended in defeats of ten lengths or more; fades flag, hold-up style pushed forward by field configuration, and the trainer's 14-day record of 1/35 offers no encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Money Shuffler
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose best efforts came over 10f-16f on STA; switched to good ground here but fades flag attached and natural hold-up style is compromised by the redistribution — the handicap mark of 45 is low but the tactical position is awkward.|

runners_data.name: Coul Dore
runners_data.note: The key horse in the pace map — sole front-runner who will get an uncontested lead; fades flag noted and has not won, but place at 10f on good ground is the key piece of form; hold-up/handily-set headgear combination with ht and a 20-day freshener.|

runners_data.name: Piatra Neamt
runners_data.note: OR 43 and the lowest-rated runner; recent form shows a fifth at 14f on good ground and some distance experience, but fades flag and hold-up nature pushed into midfield configuration make a winning run very hard to construct.|

runners_data.name: Princess Rosie
runners_data.note: All five career runs have been over 7f-10f and all have finished in the bottom half of the field on good ground; stepping to 1m5f for the first time, fades flag present, and nothing in the form to suggest the trip extension will unlock improvement.|

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: Third at 12f on good ground most recently — best placing — and trainer O'Callaghan has had three runners in the last 14 days showing activity; only four days since last run, a natural rear-runner placed mid-pack by field shape, but the recent form has a glimmer.|

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Prominent by style and one of only two horses in that category, which gives Jazz Forever a natural positional advantage; fades flag is a concern, but tracking Coul Dore throughout over a distance the six-year-old has handled (ran 3rd at 13f) suits the profile.|

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran with 2nd at 16f on good ground in the book, prominent runner and among the very few who will get their natural position in this race; reserve jockey query is worth noting, but the tactical position is strong in this pace shape.|

runners_data.name: Premier Princess
runners_data.note: Only four days since last run, tongue-tie on, and trainer Hogan is active; however this three-year-old has not finished better than fifth in five starts, fades consistently, and is a hold-up type who cannot get her preferred deep position in this crowded rear group.|

races.paceDynamic: Coul Dore is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and, with no other genuine pace-setter to pressurise her, she is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 1m5f trip on good ground at Down Royal. Jazz Forever and Lariat are the two prominent-style runners who will attempt to track close to the pace, but neither has the profile to hustle Coul Dore off her lead, meaning the early fractions are likely to be steady-to-modest rather than genuinely strong. With pace at a premium and the race almost certain to be run in a convoy shape, the decisive move will come from mid-to-late in the contest — the critical factor will be who has the fuel left to accelerate when Coul Dore's lead begins to compress, which tends to benefit prominent horses racing handy rather than true hold-up types who need cover and a strong gallop to close from deep. This field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: No More Hiding, Invincible Destiny, Premier Princess, Money Shuffler, Piatra Neamt, Flagstone Lady and Princess Rosie are all genuine rear-of-field horses who will be forced to race closer than ideal; Jazz Forever and Lariat, tracking the pace from a prominent position, are the runners best placed to exploit the uncontested lead and a controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coul Dore Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore gets a soft lead at a fair clip and the prominent trackers lack the finishing kick to peg her back.
scenarios.body: Coul Dore, uncontested on a good surface over a trip she handles, sets a controlled but honest gallop and simply has enough in reserve to repel challengers; the lack of pressing pace means she is never asked a serious question until the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Jazz Forever or Lariat tracks Coul Dore throughout and strikes with a sustained run from 2f out as the pace eases.
scenarios.body: A steady tempo suits hold-close runners who avoid traffic trouble; Jazz Forever or Lariat, racing just off the front, inherit momentum at the critical point without having to find a wide run through a bunched field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the field concertinas, allowing a well-positioned midfield runner to thread through as the stragglers stop.
scenarios.body: A truly slow early pace compresses the field and allows a mover from midfield — such as Miss Australie or Vervain, who have the distance form and going credentials — to pick up inside the final 2f when gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong and the field strings out, creating the genuine end-to-end gallop that true closers need.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given only one confirmed front-runner, but if the pace quickens enough to string out the field, a redistributed runner like Maxwell Smart or Plains Indian, forced wide of the pack, could close powerfully; the low probability reflects that the gallop is unlikely to be strong enough to set this up.

watchPoints.text: Coul Dore's uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor — watch whether Jazz Forever or Lariat press her at any stage in the first mile, because if neither does, she could hold on for longer than her fading profile suggests.

Jazz Forever and Lariat are the only two prominent runners in a 17-horse field; watch their early positioning carefully — whoever slots in directly behind Coul Dore will be in the prime spot when the race ignites from 2f out.

With 13 of 17 runners true hold-up types, there is significant risk of traffic problems and bunching in the straight — watch for Miss Australie and Vervain, who need a clear passage, being caught in traffic on the home turn.
Plains Indian returns after a 445-day absence — watch the market moves and early morning support as a guide to stable confidence, but treat any betting move with caution given the fitness unknown.

Flagstone Lady ran only four days ago and is the freshest horse in the field by recent run schedule alongside Premier Princess — watch both for any signs of fatigue from a quick turnaround on what could be a tiring surface if the good ground plays on the slow side.

races.paceDynamic: Dancing Steve is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 17, meaning he sets off virtually uncontested from the front over this 1m5f trip on Good turf at Down Royal. With no genuine rivals to press him early, he is expected to control tempo at a sustainable clip — but he carries a notable tendency to fade in the closing stages, which limits confidence in him lasting home despite the positional luxury. The field behind him is heavily stacked with hold-up types, many of whom cannot all settle at the rear as intended; Queen Of Astolat, Acanto, Rio Doce, Mullacurry Maid and others are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the race simply cannot accommodate every closer at the back. This race shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter who may stop — overwhelmingly favours resolute gallopers who can track from a prominent or close-midfield position and sustain their effort into the straight; pure hold-up horses who need a strong pace to close into will find this tempo insufficient and are likely to be flattered by their drawn positions on the map.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Fades, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Steve sets a moderate uncontested pace and weakens in the final furlong, allowing runners who tracked him from close-midfield to roll past.
scenarios.body: Dancing Steve's documented tendency to fade in the finish is most dangerous here on a stamina-testing 1m5f trip having led throughout; any runner close enough to pounce needs only to sustain their effort as the leader empties.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Produce Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle stages to string the field out and create real momentum for closers.
scenarios.body: This is harder to envisage with a single front-runner unlikely to be pressured, but if the gallop is honest and the field concertinas, genuine hold-up horses who find a clear run could pick off tired rivals; the problem is that many tagged hold-up types here are redistributed and not truly suited to coming from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Steve establishes a comfortable lead, manages his stamina, and the closers fail to close down quickly enough through the long straight.
scenarios.body: On Good ground with no rival willing to take him on, it is possible Dancing Steve conserves enough energy to hold all challengers if the tempo is genuinely slow; his fade tendency and step up in trip are the key risks, but calm conditions and a soft lead could compensate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely, bunching the field in the straight and producing a chaotic, contested finish with no clear winner profile.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses unable to get their natural position, traffic problems and a muddled pace could create a messy late scramble; lower-rated, resilient types who find daylight early in the straight benefit most from the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Dancing Steve — monitor his early sectionals closely; if he opens up a comfortable solo lead through the first half mile, the race hangs entirely on whether he fades in the final two furlongs, as he has done repeatedly in recent form.|

Connecteo and Zitkala Sa — both are close-tracking hold-up types who may naturally slot just off the pace rather than deep in the field; if either secures a prominent midfield berth behind Dancing Steve, they become the principal dangers in this pace shape.|

Queen Of Astolat, Rio Doce and Acanto — all three are genuine hold-up horses who cannot access the rear; watch if any of them drift widest in the straight to find a run, as a wide passage at 1m5f costs lengths that a slow-tempo race may not provide.|

Mystic Rose — the 7lb claim from Holohan is a real weight benefit in a race where several runners carry 130lbs-plus; if she gets a clean passage through the straight despite the positional compromise, the weight relief could make her competitive at a big price.|
